venue: Half pitch (full pitch for blocks 2, 4 and 5)
equipment: Cones (4 colours) to mark the 5 lanes
focus: In possession: occupy all 5 lanes with 2 players each, and when the full-back comes inside, the inside mid (8) goes out wide
objectives: Every player can name the 5 lanes and checks the 'two per lane' picture before receiving
Full-back inverts into the half-space and the 8 drifts wide at the same moment, creating a 2v1 on their centre mid
Find the free player (the 8 out wide, or the 6 into the 8) within 2 passes of the CB receiving
key_messages: "Two in a lane" - never three, never zero
"Who's free?" - check your shoulder before the ball arrives
"Open up" - receive on the open body, ready to play forward

blocks.title: Rondo 4v2 + pivot: find the free player

diagram.caption: x2 grids. 4 outside + 1 pivot (6) keep the ball from 2 pressers. A pass through the pressers into the pivot = 1 point.

blocks.setup: Two 15x15m grids, 8 per grid: 4 outside, 1 pivot in the middle, 2 pressers and 1 'next presser' on the line who swaps in every 45 seconds. Pressers also swap on a turnover.
how: Outside players keep the ball, max 2 touches.
Pass through the 2 pressers into the pivot = 1 point; pivot plays out to a different side = 2 points.
Pressers win it: the player who lost it swaps in.
Last 3 minutes: pivot must receive and turn in one action (open body).
blocks.link_to_theme: The pivot is the free player between the lines. It starts the session's habit: who's free, and can I find them?
coaching_points: Pivot moves into the gap between the 2 pressers, not behind one of them
Outside players receive on the open stick side, body side-on so they can see both the pivot and the next outside player
Pivot checks shoulder before the ball arrives so the first touch goes away from pressure
blocks.activity_notes: Two grids running at once. The only player not involved is the next presser, who swaps in every 45 seconds.

blocks.title: FB in, 8 out: the inversion pattern

diagram.caption: Left-side unit (x2, one each half). As LCB receives, LB steps into the half-space and the 8 drifts wide. LCB finds the free player.

blocks.setup: Full pitch split in two: one unit attacks each half. Per unit: LCB, LB, 6, 8, LW (blue) + 2 opposition in red (their winger and their centre mid) + a helper feeding from the GK area. Mark the 5 lanes with cones on the sidelines and halfway.
how: Helper feeds LCB. On the feed, LB steps inside into the half-space and the 8 drifts out to the wide lane: two per lane is kept.
Pattern A: LCB to 6, 6 opens up and plays out to the 8 wide, 8 carries into the space ahead.
Pattern B: LCB into LB on the back foot (open body), one-touch set to the 6, 6 plays the diagonal into the 8.
Rounds 1-2 unopposed at 70%, then the red W and CM go live at 50% and the LCB must pick the right pattern.
Swap to the right side after 10 minutes (RCB, RB, 6, 8, RW).
blocks.link_to_theme: The core rotation of the whole programme: FB in, 8 out keeps two per lane and creates a 2v1 against their centre mid.
coaching_points: Timing: LB and 8 move as the ball travels to the LCB, not after the LCB has received
LB receives in the half-space with an open body (shoulders facing the far side) so they can play forward or set
8 arrives wide on the blind side of their winger, who is watching the ball
LCB: if the W blocks the line to the LB, the 8 wide is the free player - play it early
questions: Their winger followed our LB inside: who is free now?
Why does the 8 have to go wide when the LB comes in?
progressions: Red CM jumps to whoever receives, live
Limit the blue unit to 2 touches each
regressions: Red players passive (stick only, no tackling)
Helper calls 'A' or 'B' to choose the pattern
blocks.activity_notes: Two units of 8 on separate halves. Red players rotate with blue every 3 reps so nobody stands for more than one rep.

blocks.title: Lane game 7v6: build out with two per lane

diagram.caption: Blue build from the halfway line and score by carrying into the circle. Red press and score in the full goal. Max 2 blue per lane.

blocks.setup: Half pitch, 5 lanes coned across the width. Blue 7 (back 4, 6, two 8s) start on the halfway line with the ball. Red 6 + GK defend the full goal. 3 spare players rotate in (one blue, two red) every 3 minutes.
how: Coach plays the ball into a blue CB on the halfway line.
Blue score 1 point by dribbling over the top of the circle (or into the circle with control); 2 points if the entry comes from the FB-in/8-out rotation.
Rule: max 2 blue in any lane when a pass is played. Coach shouts 'Three!' and the ball turns over.
Red win it: 6 seconds to score in the full goal.
blocks.link_to_theme: Takes the pattern into a live build-out where the two-per-lane rule is enforced and rewarded.
coaching_points: Scan the lane picture before you receive: who has left my lane, who do I need to replace?
Free player usually appears on the blind side of their winger
Ball speed: 2 touches maximum when we have the 2v1 on their CM
If the lane is blocked, recycle to the CB and restart the picture, don't force it
questions: When our LB stepped in, what did their CM have to decide?
progressions: Red go 7 (add a forward) so blue lose the spare man
regressions: Remove the lane turnover rule and just reward rotations with 2 points
blocks.activity_notes: All 16 outfield involved via rotation every 3 minutes, plus a GK. Quick restarts: coach has 10 balls on the halfway line.

step.space: Narrow to 45m width if blue find it too easy
step.people: Add a red striker to press the CBs (7v7) for the strongest group

blocks.title: 8v8 + GKs: lane bonus game

diagram.caption: 8v8 between the circles. In your own half, max 2 per lane. A goal from a move that used the FB-in/8-out rotation counts double.

blocks.setup: Full pitch, 8v8 + GKs. Lane cones stay out on both sidelines. Spare players (if any) rotate in every 4 minutes.
how: Every restart (goal, ball out over the back line) is a GK pass to a CB, so we build every time.
In your own half, max 2 per lane: coach whistle for a free hit to the other team if broken.
Goal from a move that included the FB-in/8-out rotation = 2 goals.
Coach freezes play once every 3-4 minutes to show a good or missed lane picture (max 30 seconds).
blocks.link_to_theme: Same rule, real game tempo: players have to find the lanes with both teams live and transitions happening.
coaching_points: Re-form the lane picture quickly after a turnover in our favour
The 8 who goes wide must be ready to receive and drive, not just stand there
Rest-defence: while the FB is inside, the 6 and CBs stay connected for the counter
progressions: Lane rule applies across the whole pitch
regressions: Add a neutral floater for the team in possession
blocks.activity_notes: Everybody plays. Ball-stocks behind each goal so the GK can restart instantly.

blocks.title: 11v11 (or numbers available): two per lane
blocks.setup: Full pitch match, normal rules. Swap bibs at 10 minutes. Coach on the halfway line with lane cones still out.
how: Normal game, no conditions except the focus.
Focus: every time a CB receives in our half, check the picture - two in each lane.
Coach counts how many FB-in/8-out rotations each team completes.
coaching_points: Look for the 2v1 on their centre mid
Timing of the rotation: as the pass travels
Celebrate finding the free player, not only goals
questions: How many times did we find the 8 out wide? What stopped it when it didn't work?

safety: Shin guards and gum shields for all
No raised hits in blocks 1-3 (small areas)
reflection_prompts: Did players move as the ball travelled, or after it arrived?
Which side (left or right) found the rotation more naturally?
Who needs one-to-one video on their lane positioning before Week 2?
